name: the hidden pattern symptom profile
description: an editorial-style symptom profile that validates the visitor, reveals a likely pattern, gives useful education, captures a lead, and routes to the final product offer.

results.label: stress drift
results.affirmation: your body does not look random. it looks overloaded, wired, and forced to keep compensating.
results.headline: your pattern leans toward stress drift
results.summary: the strongest signal in your answers is a body running hot for too long. sleep gets lighter, patience shortens, cravings spike, and small things start feeling weirdly expensive.
results.mechanism: when stress chemistry stays elevated, it can distort appetite, recovery, sleep quality, and how stable you feel from morning to night. that often feels personal when it is really a pattern.
educationBullets: stress-heavy patterns often show up as light sleep, afternoon crashes, and a shorter fuse.
the feeling of being puffy, inflamed, or reactive can rise when recovery never fully catches up.
the fix is rarely one magic move. it is usually calming the input and supporting steadier regulation.
dopamineCandies: your body is asking for less chaos, not more discipline.
validation matters because shame makes pattern recognition worse.
small regulation wins compound faster than heroic resets.
results.offerBridge: that is why the next step should feel supportive, not punishing: something simple enough to actually stick when your system is already carrying too much.

results.label: hormone friction
results.affirmation: the pattern in your answers suggests your body is not broken. it may be dealing with more friction than support.
results.headline: your pattern leans toward hormone friction
results.summary: the strongest signal in your answers is inconsistency: mood swings, disrupted sleep, bloating, cravings, and feeling unlike yourself without a clean explanation.
results.mechanism: when hormone-related signals start feeling less stable, the body can swing between high and low energy, weird hunger cues, poor sleep, and emotional volatility. people often interpret that as failure instead of feedback.
educationBullets: hormone friction can feel subtle at first: lighter sleep, more irritation, and a body that feels harder to read.
bloating and cravings often travel with the same pattern rather than being isolated problems.
consistency beats intensity when the goal is smoother daily regulation.
dopamineCandies: your symptoms make sense together, not separately.
a body that feels different is not automatically a body in decline.
support works best when it fits the rhythm you already live in.
results.offerBridge: if the goal is to feel more steady without turning your life into a full-time protocol, the right support has to be simple, predictable, and easy to repeat.

results.label: recovery debt
results.affirmation: your answers point to a body that has been spending more than it is restoring.
results.headline: your pattern leans toward recovery debt
results.summary: the strongest signal here is depletion: dragging into the day, brain fog, feeling less resilient, and noticing that your body takes longer to bounce back than it used to.
results.mechanism: recovery debt builds when sleep quality, nutritional steadiness, and daily stress stop paying you back fast enough. the result is not laziness. it is lower reserve.
educationBullets: recovery debt often looks like low motivation when the real issue is low reserve.
brain fog and low patience frequently arrive before people name the pattern as depletion.
support that lowers friction can help more than another ambitious restart.
dopamineCandies: capacity is trainable again when the baseline stops slipping.
the goal is not perfection. it is easier recovery and steadier reserve.
you do not need a harder routine. you need a more believable one.
results.offerBridge: the strongest next move is usually a low-friction support layer that helps your body feel easier to manage before you ask more from it.
